claim: PLAIN: Dhruv's ideal Trotter step is 12 copies of the same 3-qubit 'hopping' operation (each perfect at 4 entangling MS gates) plus 6 tiny 2-qubit ones (1 MS each), total 54. Our incumbent hits exactly 54 at near-perfect fidelity. To beat him we must drop ONE entangling gate (to 53) and still land within the scorer's fidelity tolerance (1e-4). EXP-0002 showed you cannot do this by shrinking ONE block in isolation to 3 MS -- its leftover error is too big. The new bet is compensation: after removing the 4th MS of one hopping block, let the FREE ANGLES of the neighboring blocks that share qubits with it soak up the resulting error. Because those neighbors touch the same qubits, a whole-circuit angle re-optimization can push the total error back down in a way per-block fitting structurally cannot. FORMAL: build the exact 54-MS incumbent from target primitives; reduce exactly one hopping block b* from its 4-MS realization to a 3-MS ansatz (warm-started from fit_block(HOP_UNITARY, hop_qubits(b*), n_ms=3)); then jointly re-optimize, via scipy L-BFGS, the native angles of b*'s 3-MS ansatz AND of every block whose qubit support overlaps b* (all disjoint blocks frozen), minimizing state-averaged mean infidelity vs U_ideal. If the global optimum reaches <= 1e-4 with margin, ship the resulting 53-MS circuit. This is Director lane 2/3 (whole-circuit angle re-optimization exploiting cross-block qubit sharing), NOT per-block pruning (EXP-0002), and it is exactly the whole-circuit-compensation probe that EXP-0002's reopen condition priced open.
prediction: A valid native circuit at 53 MS gates (11 hopping blocks x 4 MS + 1 hopping block x 3 MS + 6 on-site x 1 MS = 53) with state-averaged mean infidelity vs U_ideal <= 1e-4, promoting over the 54-MS incumbent (STRETCH: strictly below Dhruv's 9N=54). Confidence ~40%: the exact per-block minimum being 4 is strong evidence each hopping unitary genuinely needs 4 MS in isolation, but the whole-circuit manifold with shared-qubit neighbors is a strict superset of the per-block manifold, so it can only do better than EXP-0002's per-block 3-MS residual r>5e-5 -- the open question is whether neighbor compensation crosses from r>5e-5 down under 1e-4.
falsifier: After global L-BFGS re-optimization from >=3 warm-started restarts, the best converged 53-MS ansatz still has mean infidelity > 1e-4 on a FRESH independent draw of 200 mixed states (Haar / random-product / computational-basis) -- i.e., neighboring blocks' free angles cannot compensate the removed 4th MS within tolerance. Equivalently: the scorekeeper certifies the shipped 53-MS circuit as INVALID (infidelity > 1e-4) or it fails to promote.
kill_threshold: If the offline probe's best converged mean infidelity on the fresh independent draw exceeds 1e-4 (cannot even reach within 2x, i.e. > 2e-4), OR the scorekeeper's verdict is INVALID / no-promotion, then below-54 via single-block-prune + whole-circuit angle compensation is DEAD. Accept it: 54 MS stands as the honest bound and we do NOT claim Dhruv's 9N=54 is suboptimal.
brief:
EDIT ONLY workspace/candidate.py. It must define build_circuit() -> list of native-gate tuples and be SELF-CONTAINED at score time: numpy allowed; do NOT import target/baseline/incumbent (scored as a copy in experiments/ where workspace modules are absent). Run all optimization OFFLINE in workspace (where target IS importable), then freeze the resulting gate list as float literals into build_circuit.

MATCH target.apply_circuit's exact tuple format for every gate (mirror how target constructs GPi(phi)/GPi2(phi)/RZ(theta)/MS(phi0,phi1,theta) tuples and their qubit-index positions -- read target.py and copy the convention verbatim).

OFFLINE PROCEDURE (scaffolding you run to produce frozen angles; not shipped):
1. Rebuild the exact 54-MS incumbent gate list from target primitives: for each of the 12 hopping blocks b, take fit_block(HOP_UNITARY, hop_qubits(b), n_ms=4) and place it on hop_qubits(b); for each of the 6 on-site blocks i, take fit_block(INT_UNITARY, int_qubits(i), n_ms=1) on int_qubits(i). Assemble in the SAME frozen order that target.ideal_step applies (read target.py for the ordering). Sanity: assert target.ms_count==54, target.is_native==True, and estimate_infidelity < 1e-6 (should be ~1e-13). If this does not reproduce the incumbent, STOP and report -- the reconstruction is wrong.
2. Pick one hopping block b* (use the FIRST hopping block in frozen order). Replace its 4-MS sub-circuit with a 3-MS ansatz warm-started from fit_block(HOP_UNITARY, hop_qubits(b*), n_ms=3), remapped onto hop_qubits(b*). Circuit is now 53 MS: assert target.ms_count==53, target.is_native==True.
3. Free-parameter set (locality-reduced, principled): collect the angle parameters of (a) b*'s 3-MS ansatz gates, and (b) every OTHER block whose qubit support intersects hop_qubits(b*) (compute overlaps via hop_qubits(.)/int_qubits(.)). FREEZE all blocks disjoint from b* (they are on other qubits and cannot compensate; their infidelity contribution is fixed at ~0). Flatten the free angles into a vector theta0 (the warm-start values).
4. Objective J(theta): rebuild the full 53-MS circuit with the free angles set from theta, then J = mean over a FIXED sample of M=24 states psi of [1 - |<ideal_step(psi) | apply_circuit(circuit, psi)>|^2]. Sample composition: 8 Haar-random full-space (2^18) states, 8 random product states, 8 computational-basis states (use target's own state helpers if present; otherwise construct with a fixed local RNG seed). Keep the sample FIXED within a single L-BFGS run.
5. Optimize: scipy.optimize.minimize(J, theta0, method='L-BFGS-B', options={'maxiter':200}). Do >=3 restarts: restart 0 from theta0; restarts 1..k from theta0 + small Gaussian perturbation (sigma~0.05 rad) on the b*-ansatz angles, RESAMPLING the M-state objective set each restart. Keep the params with lowest J.
6. OVER-FIT GUARD (mandatory): with the best params, draw a NEW independent set of 200 mixed states (fresh RNG seed, same 3 types) and compute mean infidelity. This fresh-draw number is your advisory offline result -- report it. Do NOT tune against the hidden battery; do NOT optimize toward any single state distribution or noise realization (2022 Google SYK over-pruning trap).
7. Freeze: extract the final 53-gate list with optimized angles as float literals and write build_circuit() returning it verbatim. Shipped candidate.py = numpy import + build_circuit only (no optimizer, no target import). Assert offline once more on the shipped list that target.ms_count==53 and target.is_native==True.

SHIP the 53-MS circuit regardless of the offline fidelity outcome -- the scorekeeper's verdict on the hidden battery is what enters the ledger (Rule 3). If the offline fresh-draw infidelity is clearly hopeless (>>1e-4), still ship it so the falsifier is scored on real hidden states, and report the offline number honestly.
done_definition: workspace/candidate.py defines build_circuit() -> list of native-gate tuples that is self-contained (numpy only; no import of target/baseline/incumbent), builds a circuit with EXACTLY 53 MS gates (target.ms_count==53) that is fully native (target.is_native==True), structured as 11 hopping blocks at 4 MS + 1 hopping block (b*) at 3 MS + 6 on-site blocks at 1 MS, with all free angles set to the values found by the offline global L-BFGS re-optimization. The coder reports the offline fresh-draw (200 independent mixed states) mean infidelity as advisory. Promotion is decided solely by the scorekeeper's verdict.
reopen_condition: If this dies (best global-optimized 53-MS ansatz stays > 1e-4 on the fresh draw, or scorekeeper certifies INVALID/no-promotion), the below-54 direction reopens ONLY via a genuinely STRUCTURAL cross-block saving, not approximate pruning: identify two hopping blocks that are CONSECUTIVE in the frozen application order AND share >=1 qubit (so their ordered product on the combined 5-qubit support is exact with no intervening block on that support), form that joint 5-qubit unitary, and demonstrate in an offline fit_block(U_joint, joint_qubits, n_ms=7) probe on my own random states that its residual mean infidelity <= 1e-4 -- i.e. a qubit-sharing block PAIR compresses 8 MS -> 7 MS exactly. Priced: requires enumerating the frozen block order, finding a qualifying consecutive overlapping pair, and one 5-qubit fit, ~1 coder cycle. Retry below-54 only if such a probe shows <= 1e-4 feasible at the pair level.
